correctness.rationale: The proof begins from the source exact explicit formula, retains all prime powers, and uses its Theorem 2.4 before summation. The three summed error exponents are strictly negative under alpha<sigma/(2sigma+1). Absolute convergence at sigma+1/2>1 justifies dominated convergence and the identity -zeta'/zeta=sum Lambda(q)q^{-s}. The archimedean constant follows from Stirling and the classical off-critical second moment. Pole-evaluation terms are negligible by Paley--Wiener decay. The claimed nonuniformity follows from the Laurent expansion at s=1. Computation is explicitly non-probative.

value.rationale: The source identifies a sharp qualitative phase change at sigma=1/2 but leaves an O(1/log T) finite-height uncertainty for every fixed off-critical sigma. The exact coefficient is a natural quantitative refinement: it combines the gamma-factor constant with the full prime-power contribution in one zeta-logarithmic-derivative value, and its pole gives a concrete analytic signature of the transition. This is structurally motivated rather than an arbitrary finite specialization.
